findings.description: The fixture on line 100 now puts the file at `tests/hooks/new.test.sh`, but the case label `'a new harness under .claude/hooks/'` still names the old location; a failure would point at the wrong directory. Change it to `'a new harness under tests/hooks/'`.

`case $file in scripts/* | tests/* | .github/workflows/*) harnesses=true` runs every shell harness on any change under `tests/`. In an adapted project with its own test tree there (e.g. pytest's `tests/test_x.py`), every project-test change then runs minutes of shell harnesses (no `--affected`). Narrowing it to `tests/scripts/* | tests/hooks/*` keeps coverage for harness helpers without that cost.

The verification step `bash -n .claude/hooks/*.sh scripts/*.sh` used to syntax-check the harnesses because they lived under those globs. After the move it checks none of them; add `tests/*/*.test.sh` to restore that coverage.

The pairing of harness directory to subject directory is written in three places: the `affects()` case branches (`tests/scripts/*) subject=scripts/...`, `tests/hooks/*) subject=.claude/hooks/...`), the glob on line 76, and the header comment. A new harness directory that gets a glob but no case branch makes `--affected` skip it silently. One `dir:subject` pair list could drive both the globs and the lookup.
